citation: Kolotouros, Wallden (2022). Evolving objective function for improved variational quantum optimization. Physical Review Research 4, 023225.
verified_via: Crossref DOI + arXiv API; full text read (LLM-assisted extraction; headline grep-checked)
objective: Ascending-CVaR: at iteration t, CVaR_{alpha_t} = (1/ceil(alpha_t*K)) * sum_{k=0}^{ceil(alpha_t*K)} H_k (average of the lowest ceil(alpha_t*K) sampled energies), where alpha_t is increased over the course of optimisation according to an ascending schedule (linear: alpha_{t+1}=alpha_t+lambda; or sigmoid: alpha_t = 1/(1+e^{5-lambda*t})), starting from a small alpha_0 and ending at alpha=1 (full expectation value) or truncated earlier.
ansatz: Two ansatze tested: (1) VQE with hardware-efficient ansatz, depth p=1 only: qubits initialised in |0>, each layer = Ry(theta_i) rotations on every qubit + CZ_{ij} gates for i<j; number of parameters mu = n(1+p). (2) QAOA, depth p=1 to p=6, standard cost-unitary e^{-i*gamma*H_C} alternating with mixer e^{-i*beta*H_B} (H_B=sum sigma_x), initial state |+>^n (uniform superposition), 2p parameters.
optimiser: COBYLA (gradient-free), same optimiser used for all problems/instances; random initial parameters (same initial parameters used across different alpha choices for fair comparison).
hyperparameters: Linear ascending factor lambda in [0.025, 0.045]; sigmoid ascending factor lambda in [0.3, 0.4]; alpha_0 = 0.01 initial value; shots K=1000 scaled to K/alpha_t per iteration; max optimiser iterations = 66 x (number of ansatz parameters); comparison fixed-alpha baselines: alpha = 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1 (expectation value); success threshold defined as >=10% overlap with optimal solution; QAOA depths p=1..6, VQE depth p=1 only; problem sizes 15-20 qubits.
benchmark: Three QUBO-mapped combinatorial problems via classical (noiseless) Qiskit Aer simulation: Max-Cut (unweighted non-regular random graphs, 15-19 vertices, 100 instances), Number Partitioning (17-20 integers drawn from sets N1={0..200}, N2={0..500}, N3={0..750}, 300 instances total), Portfolio Optimisation (16-20 assets, 100 random portfolios with random budget and risk factor q).
headline_result: Success (>=10% overlap with optimum): Max-Cut 96% Ascending-CVaR vs 84% (a=0.1), 81% (a=0.2), 53% (mean energy); Number Partitioning hardest set 95% vs ~60% best constant CVaR; Portfolio 100% (as a=0.1/0.2) vs 1% (mean). Mean overlap with optimum up to ~10x higher than mean-energy objective (Table IV).
reproduce_in_exact_sim: Loss of p(x) only. Reuse exact-CVaR engine (gradient = adjoint with diagonal observable h_x=min(E_x-VaR_a,0)/a); add outer loop over a_t (linear a_{t+1}=a_t+lambda, lambda 0.025-0.045 from a0=0.01, or sigmoid a_t=1/(1+exp(5-lambda t)), lambda 0.3-0.4) with warm-started L-BFGS-B per stage. Finite shots: scale K->K/a_t. Effort: low.

citation: Li, Fan, Coram et al. (2020). Quantum optimization with a novel Gibbs objective function and ansatz architecture search. Physical Review Research 2, 023074.
verified_via: Crossref DOI + arXiv API; full text read (LLM-assisted extraction; headline grep-checked)
objective: Gibbs objective function: f = -log<e^{-ηE}>, where the expectation is taken over the Born distribution of the output quantum state and E is the diagonal cost Hamiltonian. This replaces the standard QAOA objective <E> (energy expectation value). η is a fixed hyperparameter estimated as η ≈ (E0 - Egs)^{-1}, with E0=0.95*Egs used in experiments giving η≈20.
ansatz: QAOA circuit at p=1: |ψ> = e^{iβX}e^{iγE} H^⊗n|0^n>, with two-qubit ZZ-type gates for eiγE placed on edges of an instance graph G_I (Ising model). Also studies a "sparse ansatz" found via Ansatz Architecture Search (AAS): same QAOA-like circuit but with some two-qubit gates (edges) removed from G_I to form a sparser ansatz graph G_A, searched via greedy/beam search removing up to 20 edges.
optimiser: Nelder-Mead (blackbox optimizer) used to optimize β,γ minimizing either <E> or the Gibbs objective f. Initial β,γ sampled from U(0,0.1). For AAS scoring, also explored analytical/estimated and fixed parameter prescriptions, and heuristic scoring (random, energy-approximation, neural network) to avoi
hyperparameters: η (Gibbs inverse temperature) ≈ 20, derived from η=(E0-Egs)^{-1} with E0=0.95*Egs, Egs≈-1. QAOA depth p=1 (2 parameters β,γ). AAS: greedy search (beam width w=1) or beam search with various w (found w≥1 gives little extra improvement), searching up to n=20 removed edges. Nelder-Mead initial parameters ~U(0,0.1). Neural network scoring: 2 dense layers, 128 hidden units, ReLU; trained on 800 instances (232,800 ansatzes for grid, 568,800 for complete graph), tested on 200 held-out instances; beam width w=100 for heuristic scoring methods. Noise model: depolarizing probability p analyzed analytically relating Δf≈p.
benchmark: Ising models: (1) 4x4 grid, 16 vertices, 24 edges, avg degree 3; (2) complete graph with 10 vertices, 45 edges, degree 9 each. Couplings J_ij ~ U(-1,1). 1000 instances each. Success metric: P(E<0.95*Egs(I)) computed exactly from the wavefunction (exact statevector, no sampling).
headline_result: QAOA+Gibbs gives 10.8% (grid) and 8.6% (complete graph) median relative improvement in P(E<0.95Egs) vs QAOA+energy baseline. Combining Gibbs objective with AAS-found sparse ansatz gives 44.4% (grid) and 244.7% (complete graph) median relative improvement in P(low energy), with 20.8% and 33.3% median reduction in number of two-qubit gates, respectively.
reproduce_in_exact_sim: Loss of p(x): L=-log sum_x p(x) exp(-eta(E_x-E_ref)); adjoint with diagonal observable h_x=exp(-eta(E_x-E_ref)) times -1/sum(p h). Use log-sum-exp with E_ref = best energy seen. Paper's eta=20 is for O(1) Ising energies (eta~1/(E0-Egs), E0=0.95Egs); for us set eta*(E_2nd-E_opt) ~1-5 on the feasible spectrum and anneal eta upwards. Large-eta limit approaches -log P(opt). Effort: low.

verified_via: Crossref DOI + arXiv API; full text read (LLM-assisted extraction)
objective: CVaR_alpha(X(theta)) = (1/ceil(alpha*K)) * sum_{k=0}^{ceil(alpha*K)} H_k, where H_k are sorted (nondecreasing) sampled diagonal Hamiltonian values (QUBO objective evaluations) from measurement outcomes of |psi(theta)>; replaces the expected value min_theta <psi(theta)|H|psi(theta)> as the classical-optimizer objective. Limit alpha->0 gives the min sample; alpha=1 gives the expectation.
ansatz: CVaR-VQE: layer of single-qubit Y-rotations on all n qubits, then p repetitions of {all-to-all controlled-Z gates on all pairs i<j, followed by a layer of Y-rotations}; n(1+p) parameters, n(n-1)p/2 CZ gates, depth O(np). Depths tested p=0,1,2. On hardware: nearest-neighbor (ring) entanglement instead of all-to-all, p=0,1,2, initial parameters fixed to theta=0. CVaR-QAOA: standard QAOA ansatz (Hadamard layer + alternating UC(gamma) cost-unitary / UB(beta) mixer) with depth p=1,2,3, only 2p parameters.
optimiser: COBYLA (classical, gradient-free)
hyperparameters: alpha in {1%, 5%, 10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%} swept in simulation; alpha in {10%,25%,100%} on hardware. VQE depth p=0,1,2; QAOA depth p=1,2,3. 8,192 shots per trial on hardware, 5 repeated runs per setting. Number of normalized iterations up to 50 (simulation) / up to ~140 (hardware). 340 random instances x 14,280 test cases total in simulation sweep. Portfolio problem params: n=6 assets, q=0.5, budget B=3, penalty lambda=12.
benchmark: Six CO problem classes: maximum stable set, max-3-SAT, number partitioning, maximum cut, market split, portfolio optimization; 10 random instances each at 6,8,10,12,14,16 qubits (Max3Sat: 6,9,12,15 qubits). Hardware demo: 6-qubit portfolio optimization instance on IBM Q Poughkeepsie (qubits 5,6,7,10,11,12 in a ring).
headline_result: Simulation: CVaR-VQE with p=2, alpha=1% reaches >=1% probability of sampling an optimal solution for almost all instances within 50 normalized iterations, versus only ~60% of test problems reaching the same threshold with alpha=100% (plain expectation). On hardware (6-qubit portfolio problem, VQE p=1), alpha=10%,25% runs reach/exceed their alpha-level probability of sampling the optimum in all 5 runs, while alpha=100% stays near flat/close to zero probability throughout 100 iterations. citation: Lee, Lau (2025). Solving Constrained Combinatorial Optimization Problems with Variational Quantum Imaginary Time Evolution. arXiv:2504.12607 (preprint).
verified_via: arXiv API; full text read (LLM-assisted extraction)
objective: min_x -Σ_i Σ_j v_j x_ij - λ1[Σ_i h1^(i)(x) + Σ_j h2^(j)(x)] + λ2[Σ_i h1^(i)(x)^2 + Σ_j h2^(j)(x)^2], i.e. unbalanced-penalization QUBO (2nd-order Taylor approx. of e^{-h(x)} penalty for each inequality constraint), converted to an equivalent Max-Cut Hamiltonian H_MaxCut = -Σ_(i,j) <Z_iZ_j> + m/2 via QUBO→Max-Cut mapping (n variables → n+1 vertices). VarQITE minimizes the McLachlan distance θ̇ = argmin_θ ||(d/dτ + H - E_τ)|ψ(θ)>|| ⇔ solves M θ̇ = V linear system (M_ij=Re[∂<ψ|/∂θ_i ∂|ψ>/∂θ_j], V_i=-Re[∂<ψ|/∂θ_i H|ψ>]).
ansatz: iHVA (imaginary Hamiltonian Variational Ansatz): sequence of two-qubit RZY(θ)=e^{-iθZ_iY_j/2} (and alternating RYZ) gates placed along edges of a breadth-first spanning tree of the Max-Cut graph; tree edges removed and process repeated until all edges covered; p rounds give p|E| parameters. All ansatzes (iHVA, ma-QAOA, HEA) use 1 repetition. Compared baselines: HEA and multi-angle QAOA (ma-QAOA), 1 rep, optimized with BFGS (not QITE).
optimiser: VarQITE parameter update via McLachlan variational principle + Euler integration (θ(τ0+Δτ)=θ(τ0)+θ̇Δτ), solving linear system M θ̇=V at each step (no classical gradient-descent optimizer used for QITE). For VQE baselines (iHVA w/o QITE, ma-QAOA, HEA): BFGS classical optimizer.
